reason: The passage consistently portrays Yahweh as transcendent and distant: God appears on a cloud-covered mountain, maintains physical separation from the Israelites (who stand at a distance), communicates through intermediaries (Moses), and the people fear direct encounter with God, saying 'Let not God speak with us, lest we die' (וְאַל־ יְדַבֵּ֥ר עִמָּ֛נוּ אֱלֹהִ֖ים פֶּן־ נָמֽוּת). The 'all-powerful' aspect is evident throughout: Yahweh demonstrates mighty acts against Egypt, carries Israel 'on eagles' wings,' claims dominion over 'all the earth' (כִּי־ לִ֖י כָּל־ הָאָֽרֶץ), speaks from heaven itself (מִן־ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי עִמָּכֶֽם), and establishes covenant unilaterally with absolute authority. While the passage does show relational elements (covenant, blessing), these are structured hierarchically with clear divine supremacy and distance maintained throughout.
